overview: Dominica is a small island country in the eastern Caribbean. Its capital is Roseau. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1978. Dominica is home to the Kalinago, the only Indigenous people in the eastern Caribbean who still live on their own territory. It is a different country from the Dominican Republic.

geography.text: Dominica is mountainous and covered in rainforest, which has earned it the nickname 'the Nature Isle of the Caribbean'. It is a volcanic island, with hot springs and the Boiling Lake, a flooded vent that bubbles with volcanic heat. Heavy rainfall feeds its many rivers and waterfalls.

history.text: Dominica's Kalinago people kept European settlers out longer than almost anywhere else in the Caribbean. France and Britain fought over the island until it became British in the late 1700s. Dominica became independent in 1978, and in 2017 Hurricane Maria caused enormous damage.

events.title: Kalinago Territory
events.text: Land is set aside for the Kalinago people.

events.title: Hurricane Maria
events.text: The hurricane damages almost every building on the island.

government.text: Dominica is a parliamentary republic within the Commonwealth. Parliament elects the President as head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government. It became independent from Britain in 1978.

economy.text: Dominica's economy relies on farming, especially bananas, and on eco-tourism. It sells citizenship to foreign investors, which brings in a large share of government income. Hurricanes, especially Maria in 2017, have caused huge damage.

culture.text: Dominica is called the 'Nature Isle of the Caribbean', with rainforest, waterfalls and the Boiling Lake, a flooded volcanic vent. It is home to the Kalinago, one of the few remaining Indigenous Caribbean communities, who live in their own territory.

items.title: Boiling Lake
items.text: The world's second-largest hot lake, in a volcanic crater.

items.title: Kalinago Territory
items.text: Land set aside for the Kalinago people in 1903.

sport.text: Cricket is the most popular sport, and Dominica plays as part of the West Indies team. Thea LaFond won Dominica's first Olympic medal, a gold in the triple jump, in 2024.

items.text: Thea LaFond won Olympic gold in the triple jump.

didYouKnow: Dominica has 365 rivers, according to local tradition.
The Boiling Lake is the second-largest hot lake in the world.
